items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oh, my God. All right. Thank you, Mary. Goodbye.

ctx.x: Well, it was true in the early days of the Austin Band. There's no question about it. When they really didn't know what they were playing.

Well, I'm sure that it arose from a number of experiments, and some of these features do seem... Oh, my God. All right. Thank you, Mary. Goodbye. Goodbye. I'm sure that... You were talking about dynamics before...

Well, I was talking about the Wolverines and the effect that they had on the Austin boys, as far as a conscious feeling on tempo. And the breaks, which were important things at that stage of the game, were used that way. The rule in the Wolverines used to be that any break you took had to not only sustain the rhythm but improve it. And the result was, if you go back and play those Wolverine records with that idea in mind, you'll understand that's exactly what all of them were doing. Bob Gillette, the guitar…
